data.title: Denial of Service via Resource Exhaustion or Service Stop
data.summary: The sample stops or disables a targeted service or process, or exhausts local resources, denying availability of a specific function rather than destroying data.
data.description:
This is a narrower, often more surgical action than a wiper: stopping a specific backup
agent, database service, or security product's service so that whatever depends on it
stops functioning, without touching the data those services manage. It is frequently a
supporting step for a different primary objective (disabling backup software ahead of
ransomware, stopping a security service ahead of further activity) rather than the
sample's main purpose.
data.recommendation:
* Identify which specific service or process was targeted and treat it as a signal of the sample's actual objective — disabling backup or security services points to a further stage still coming.
* Restart and verify the integrity of the stopped service once the sample is contained; stopping rarely corrupts the service's own data.
* Alert on service-stop or process-termination targeting backup and security-product services specifically, given how rarely this is legitimate.
data.short_recommendation: Identify the specific service stopped — it is often a supporting step revealing the sample's real, further objective.

mitre_techniques.procedure: Issued a service-control stop request against the host's backup agent service immediately before the ransomware stage began encrypting files.

mbc_techniques.implementation: Stopped a targeted service via the service control manager rather than exhausting resources generically.
